utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody. May we please hear the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. This is Case Number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And the appearances, please, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Nicholas Koumjian, Ann Sutherland, and Ruth Karper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Branko Lukic and John Ostojic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. May we go, please, for one minute into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I should like to have comments on the 92 bis, 94 bis statements, especially the new one Defence requested for admission. Also only by Monday. Beforehand, we can't resolve any problems. We are aware that one of the envisaged witnesses for next week has been cancelled. Therefore, it might be not that problem in case we can't conclude with the last witness scheduled for this week. We would in addition like to hear comments on the admission of the new exhibits arriving, having arrived this week. But this can also be done only next Monday. Then the question of the time of today's hearing and tomorrow's hearing. We will sit today from 9.00 to 12.00, and then from 1.30 to 4.30 today -- this will be tomorrow, 6 March, 9.00 to 12.00, 1.30 to 4.30. The 5th of March, that is today, 9.00 to 10.30, 11.00 to 12.00, 1.30 to 2.30, 2.45 to 1500, this is ex parte under Rule 66(C) as foreseen under the rules. I would ask the parties to give an answer to the question whether the translations, the necessary translations, have been exchanged. Are there any gaps? And finally, we are aware that Mr. Milorad Loncar, in fact, was in the list of the witnesses under 92 bis. It was discussed at that point in time. One of the reasons why not to hear Mr. Milorad Loncar, that it would be a witness being repetitive, opposed to another priest who apparently has not got the necessary license or admission to testify in this case. But the Defence should know that up to this moment, we do not know when Dr. Stakic met this Milorad Loncar, on which occasion, for what purposes, and what is the relevance for our case. We are prepared to revisit this question because the ruling at that time was primarily based on the repetitiveness of this witness. This is no longer the case. But as long as we don't have any additional data justifying the calling of another witness, we can't decide on this. So we expect also here a written additional comment. Any other urgent matters for this morning? This seems not to be the case. So may I ask the usher to escort the witness into the courtroom, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Budimir. You are prepared to continue --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: -- To continue with your testimony? May I ask the usher to distribute the transcript Exhibit S91-1. It's already done. Then may I ask the at this time audio-unit to play the tape. And may I ask you, Mr. Budimir, to listen to this tape that will be played only in those parts, for the parties, to be found on pages transcript 5797 through 5823.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Stop. Can you hear who is speaking on this audiotape?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure, but I assume that this is the voice of Mr. Miskovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So I would kindly ask you, when you are sure that you have identified the one or other voice, please say stop immediately. All right? Can we proceed this way?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's okay if I can follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Stop. Have you now some clarification for yourself, are we listening to the voice of whom? Is it, in fact, Mr. Miskovic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it is Mr. Miskovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And when we just heard "then I scheduled a Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. meeting of the Crisis Staff for 2.00 a.m.," does it in any way change your testimony when the first meeting of the Crisis Staff was held?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. Then let's continue, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Stop. You have heard the reporter making reference to Mr. Simo Drljaca. Once again the question: Are you sure the voice we just listened to was not Mr. Drljaca but Mr. Miskovic? Correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am more positive that this is the voice of Mr. Miskovic than I am that this is the voice of Mr. Drljaca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May we then proceed, please, with the tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Stop. May I ask you, are you able to identify the voice you are just hearing?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this is the voice of Mr. Kuruzovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue with the tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Stop. Would you like to add something to your testimony of yesterday and the day before yesterday?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In connection with what I have just heard?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Right. The answer is not yet on the transcript. If you could please repeat.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue with the tape to be played.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Stop. This concludes this part of the audiotape. My last question to you, do you have, having heard this, any amendments to your testimony of yesterday or today to make, especially related to the meeting in Cirkin Polje?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I stand by my statement, by my testimony, that I arrived in Cirkin Polje around 4.30 p.m., that the situation was very chaotic and after that we went to our respective jobs. The gentleman mentions here there had been lists of people who were unable to enter the premises. However, in the agency where I worked, I never received a list, a blacklist of people, who were not allowed to enter the premises where I was working. And all the employees who showed up for work that morning were able to enter the premises of the secretariat for national defence and go to their jobs. None of the employees of the secretariat which I headed had a problem coming into the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Is it still your testimony that the first meeting of the Crisis Staff was held after the 20th of May 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the official Crisis Staff - and I don't know what Mr. Miskovic is talking about - but the official Crisis Staff was set up pursuant to a decision by the president or the presidency - I don't know which - and signed by the president. And it was set up after the 20th. I believe there had been a session of the assembly. We discussed the dates yesterday. And I stand by my view that the Crisis Staff was established and started working after the 20th of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. It's now for the Defence to put their questions to the witness. Please, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Budimir.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As you know, I am Branko Lukic representing the accused, together with Mr. Ostojic. I will start from this last transcript of a radio programme that we have heard today. First of all, I would like to ask you this: Did you know about the existence of other Crisis Staffs in Prijedor Municipality in the spring and summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you know about the existence of the SDS Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After this, I would like to try to go through the transcripts of the previous two days when you were answering the questions of the Judges who invited you to testify in the first place. While doing this, I will quote certain numbers denoting pages and numbers of the transcript. I'm saying this so that you should not be confused when it comes to that. This is only done so that our learned friends from the OTP and the Trial Chamber are able to follow. If you do not know the answer to a question, please feel free to answer "I don't know." On page 27, 126 of that day of the trial, that is, Monday, you were talking about the session of the assembly of the Serbian Municipality of Prijedor which elected the officials of the Executive Board of the Assembly of the Serbian People of the Prijedor Municipality. You said that it was in the first half or the -- the first half of April or mid-April. Are you aware that at that time, that is, in mid-April 1992, the breakup of the legal system of Bosnia and Herzegovina was already complete?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my testimony, I said that from the beginning of 1992, in the organ that employed me, we did not apply the current regulations. We were not applying the current regulations. And I have complete information about this aspect. And generally speaking, it was common knowledge that in all areas of social life, laws and regulations were not being applied, but I don't have all the facts in order to be able to give you a very precise answer on other scores. All I know is the area of defence which was regulated by the law of national defence and the law on the army. I assert that as of 1991 in the area where I worked, these laws were not being applied.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that the Muslim/Croat presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina carried out a mobilisation of the Territorial Defence as early as the 8th of April 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the date when the mobilisation was carried out by the presidency or whatever this organ was called. But I know that the TO was mobilised and that some other units were formed within the framework of those preparations. But I have no precise information about dates and times, and I cannot answer you precisely when that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that at that time in the presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Serbian people were not represented?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they were not. But I cannot remember the exact course of events, what happened when, because in view of my job, I was not aware of what was going on at the federal level, at the level of the state of Bosnia and Herzegovina. But I believe that certain members, Serbian members of the presidency, had already walked out by that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that at that time, that is, in mid-April 1992, in more than 50 per cent of Bosnia and Herzegovinian municipalities, the conflict had already started, more precisely in 58 municipalities?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the number of municipalities --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: There's an objection by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Well, the objection is the form of the question. It presumes facts that are not in evidence. "Do you know that..." If it's not true and the witness said "no," it implies that this is an established fact. The question is leading and presumes facts not in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask the Defence, do you have some documents in support of your question? Because I don't recall, please help me if I am wrong, that we have something on this as evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Both is true, Your Honour. The truth is that there is Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. such evidence, but because of late translations, I'm aware that Your Honours are not familiar with the evidence because this evidence is offered by the Defence. And this is the set of the documents that have been translated recently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But the witness answered so he is not aware, so I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. And in similar cases, when you're aware that we have not had this possibility to go through those exhibits, please put your question in the form of a real question and not -- give the answer by questioning. I'm just discussing with Mr. Lukic only.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Budimir, this question was addressed to me, plus instructions, but if you have something to add, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you allow me, as far as I remember, I said I have no information or precise data about that. And I'm only stating the facts of which I really know and which I have official records. I have some knowledge about this as a normal citizen from the press and other sources, but I cannot rely on that in my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At the session held in mid-April, I'm talking now about the session of the Assembly of the Serbian People of Prijedor Municipality, was it ever said when you would take your office, was it linked to a particular date, or was your election conditional upon other things?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I said in my testimony to His Honour the Presiding Judge that it was in no way determined when I would take up my office. And I don't remember that it had ever been said when and how and under what conditions. Only the nominees were chosen for these posts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After this session, did you go back to your job and continued working as usual?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did continue in the job that I did before.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On page 32 of the 126th day of trial, line 3, His Honour Judge Schomburg asked you whether you had been issued with a new document enabling you to enter the premises where you worked. Since in the course of this trial, the issue arose frequently of new documents being issued, I have to ask you whether you had been issued then with an ID, a personal ID, which is an identification document that every regular citizen has? Did you get a new ID?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already answered that I don't remember that I had been issued with any new document. And especially not the document of the kind you mention.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is only an additional question. Of course I accept the answer you already gave to the Trial Chamber. Do you remember when you obtained a new personal ID after the takeover? Was it several years after?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I have my ID with me. I can produce it and show you when it was issued. I don't remember when I got it. Maybe 1994, 1995. If you allow me, I'll produce it right now and tell you the date of issue. It was issued on the 13th of May, 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would the usher please be so kind and place this ID on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Budimir, can you see on the screen this document?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is this your ID?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you be so kind as to read when it was issued.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Date of issue, 13th of May, 1997. Registration number 1619/97. Valid for ten years.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: By which agency was it issued?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Ministry of the Interior of the Republika Srpska, public security station of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember perhaps whether you had changed your ID between April and May 1997?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will no longer need this document. On page 34 on the 126th day of trial, line 10, His Honour Judge Schomburg asked you who else was replaced in the municipality of Prijedor. You answered that only officials were replaced. You also said that Mr. Medunjanin failed to show up for work on that day. From the takeover up to the beginning of armed conflicts in Prijedor Municipality, was anybody fired in your agency?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After the beginning of war, conflicts, did some people stop coming to work?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the names of the people who stopped coming to work, some of them at least?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Dzevad Habibovic, Mr. Burazovic, Mr. -- he worked in the electronic communications centre but I can't remember his name. I believe that his name was Ekrem but I'm not sure. I can't remember actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like now the exhibit --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I've just remembered. The name is Kerim. I've just remembered the gentleman's name.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like the Exhibit S141 to be shown to the witness, please. I'm sorry, we'll come back to this document because I didn't mark exactly the line.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You were saying that at one point, the military territorial body took over everything that was connected with mobilisation. Was that body a different body from your secretariat of national defence?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was different because the secretariat for national defence is a civilian organ formed by the Municipal Assembly in accordance with the law on defence whereas the military territorial organ was established by the army. Its purpose was to perform identical tasks, but the difference is in the establishment and in the body which established this organ.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you now tell us who established this military territorial body?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was established by the former JNA as a subordinate unit. It was established by the Prijedor garrison, and the offices of that military territorial organ were in the barracks. And some of the people who worked in the secretariat for national defence opted to join that military territorial organ. I did not want to do that. I decided to stay working for my agency.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were also talking about the moment when a mobilisation was taken over by some other organ from the military territorial organ and that this happened at the session on the 15th of May 1991 of the National Defence Council. Was it discussed at the time that these tasks should be taken over by the defence council of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor or alternatively that these tasks should be returned to the secretariat for defence of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the session, it was discussed that these tasks that were performed by the military territorial organ should be returned to the municipal secretariat for national defence as it was the case before these tasks had been taken over by the military territorial defence. Why the military territorial defence, i.e., the army, took over these jobs is the fact that in 1991, the secretariat did not abide by the rules but just obeyed orders that arrived in the body, in the -- to the officials of the body.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When it comes to carrying out regulations and performing the tasks Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. and the role of the secretariat for national defence of the municipality of Prijedor, did Mr. Medunjanin play a role?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it comes to the performance of tasks of a certain organ, the person who is the head of that organ is responsible for the performance of those tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like to move on to another topic which was mentioned on page 60 of the 126th day of this trial when you were talking about the building of the municipality and meetings of the Crisis Staff. Do you remember that during the attack on Prijedor which took place on the 30th of May 1992, there was a sniper fire on the building of the municipality and that shots were fired into the offices of the president, the vice-president, the small conference room?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Objection. Counsel is leading the witness and suggesting answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like to clarify now. Am I in cross-examination, Your Honour, and whether the leading questions are forbidden in cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: May I clarify my objection. I did use the wrong words. The question was "do you remember" and I did forget -- I don't know if this is cross-examination or not because of Mr. Budimir's unique status as a Court witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It is only for as you have seen in the invitation by this Chamber. The witness is a Chamber witness and it is for the parties to put questions not in the framework of examination and cross-examination, but it is just to put additional questions to the witness, because the witness is a witness under Rule 98. The basis for not allowing this question is the mere fact, and this was the second part of the objection by the Prosecution, that in fact the answer was put to the witness. And the question should be always phrased in a way "was it" or "do you remember," allowing the witness to give an answer. So therefore, please rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Budimir, do you remember the attack on Prijedor which took place on the 30th of May 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether there was fire being opened on the municipal building?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. On that evening and on that night, I found myself in the early warning and reporting centre, which is in the basement, and I remember there was fire opened from automatic weapons on the building of the Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that this caused the breaking of the glass on the windows of this building?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Bullets entered the offices on the first floor, and there were traces of bullets on the walls of these offices.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that as a result of that, meetings after this date - I know that you were a member of several bodies, so do you remember that meetings of the Crisis Staff after this were held in the basement of the building of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that meetings were held in the hall which was adjacent to the office of the president of the Municipal Assembly, and that in the basement, there was an early warning and reporting centre whose role was as I've already stated. Whether after this attack, after a day or after this attack any sessions were held down there in the basement, I can't remember. But I believe that this situation calmed very soon, and that after that, there were no other sessions held in the basement. I am not ruling out the possibility that on the following day and the day after that, sessions may have been held in the basement for the reason that you have stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like the usher to show the witness Exhibit Number 180, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 65 of the 126th day of trial, you were asked something about item 97 which begins at the top of page 69. I'm going to ask you, Mr. Budimir, whether you remember that the Territorial Defence of Republika Srpska was abolished on the 12th of April 1992 pursuant to a decision of the assembly of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that the Territorial Defence was abolished pursuant to a decision of the assembly which was forwarded by the competent command for implementation. But I can't remember the exact date, so I cannot confirm that this indeed is the date that you have mentioned. Again, I cannot establish that for a fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The conclusion that we are talking about was passed on the 29th of May 1992. I apologise. I have misled you. I should have asked you whether you remember that the Territorial Defence of Republika Srpska was abolished on the 12th of May 1992, but still you remember -- you don't remember?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, my answer would be the same regardless of the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If we assume that the 12th of May 1992 is the date when the Territorial Defence of Republika Srpska was indeed abolished, what was the importance of the discussion on that issue that took place on the 29th of May 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say that because I think there was no point discussing that because it was a decision made by a superior organ that should have been implemented. What could have been discussed was the way the decision was to be implemented. We could only ratify what a superior body had already decided. We could only discuss how to implement a decision by a superior body; nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In order that we don't have to come back, when mentioning "superior body," what do you mean by this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I mentioned a superior body, I mean -- if we're talking about a brigade, then the superior body is a corps. And if I mention a municipal assembly, then I believe that the superior body is a national assembly. And if I mention the president of the municipality, then I believe that the superior person is the president of the state. And if I talk about myself as the secretary of the secretariat, then my superior is the Ministry of Defence. So this is what I mean when I mention the word "superior." I'm talking about the body that another body is reporting to. That is what I mean when I say "superior."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like now the usher to show the witness Document 141. It's on the 59th page of the English version and on the 44th page of the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Budimir, would you please look at the first page of this document. You will find it on your left-hand side. Can you please read the heading so we know what this is all about.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Minutes of the 16th session of the Assembly of the Serbian People of Bosnia and Herzegovina held on the 12th of May in Banja Luka."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Kindly read the passage in the top part of page 44.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The English version, page 59.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the purpose of me reading this is. I don't have any information on that. I've already stated that in political terms, I cannot give you my judgement of the decisions of an organ. And I will -- I will do what you tell me to do, Your Honours, if you think I should read I will. But I don't know whether there's any point in me reading because I cannot give any assessment of something that I haven't seen before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: If the Defence can focus on a concrete portion, and then I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's only one paragraph on the top of the page 44 in B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. So as we proceeded in the past in the same way, please be so kind to read it out loudly, and then if possible, comment on this as requested by the Defence counsel. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Still we have to adopt these amendments. Who is in favour? Who is against? Abstaining? This means that the amendments to the constitution have been adopted. Precede, please. A participate in the discussion. At the session held on 12 May 1992, it adopted a law on amendments to the National Defence act. Article 1: In the National Defence act, Official Gazette number 4/92, in all the provisions of the act, the terms "Territorial Defence" and "armed forces" shall be replaced by the following words: "The Serbian Republic of the BH army." "Article 2: Subsection 2 of the article 10 is hereby expunged. It is an article in the subsection which regulated something concerning Territorial Defence. "Article 3: Articles 37 to 53 also have to do with Territorial Defence and are hereby expunged. "Article 4: This act shall enter into effect eight days from its publication in the Official Gazette of the Serbian people of Bosnia-Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question, Mr. Budimir, is as follows: Was this session competent to change the law that we were reading about?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The competencies of this assembly should be discussed by those who were the leaders of that assembly. I told you that I just implemented the laws that I was supposed to implement. This assembly and this part here were established in the way they were established. We all know that this was the assembly of the Serbian People which was legitimate and legal in the given situation. And I don't want to go into talking about any broader, more general aspects of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I've told you, if whenever you feel you don't know something, you are more than welcome to say "I don't know." My question is whether we can now conclude that the Crisis Staff did not have any authority to abolish the Territorial Defence in any of its parts, including the Territorial Defence of the municipality of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not use the word "authority." I would use the word "competency." And in accordance with the laws that were in effect, the Crisis Staff did not have the authority or the competency to abolish the Territorial Defence in the territory of the Municipality of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would it be a convenient time now, Your Honour, or I should proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You may proceed 5 more minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When we're talking about the Territorial Defence, I would like to ask you to help us with something and explain to us how the units of the Territorial Defence were divided into the manoeuvre units and territorial units.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The territorial units of the Territorial Defence were in charge of controlling the territories of municipalities by providing security to facilities and roads, and they were set up in local communes and in companies and institutions. In companies and institutions, territorial units were somehow connected with the existing guard services of the respective units and companies. As for the manoeuvre units, the word says that these units were active not only in a certain territory but they could be used in a broader area outside the territory of a certain municipality in keeping with the orders of the superior commands.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was the 5th Kozara Brigade a unit of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In accordance with the development plans of the Territorial Defence, it developed as a manoeuvre unit of the Territorial Defence. And it was resubordinated to the JNA; that is, to the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was it customary for the so-called manoeuvre units to be resubordinated to the army even in the peacetimes? Or did it only happen when the immediate war threat was declared? Could you tell us something about that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already told you that all the units, their preparations and plans for development, and their replenishment of these units was done by the Territorial Defence. There was the municipal staff of the Territorial Defence, there was the district staff of the Territorial Defence, and there was also national staff of the Territorial Defence. When the immediate threat of war was declared, these units were immediately resubordinated to army units. Unlike this Territorial Defence, which was established on the Territorial Defence which was established on the territorial principle and was resubordinated to the army units later on, as I have already said in my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the 5th Kozara Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Pero Colic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what was Mr. Kuruzovic's function or position?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Kuruzovic was appointed the commander of the municipal staff of Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When it comes to the appointment of the municipal staff of the Territorial Defence, did the Municipal Assembly play a role?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did play a role. The Municipal Assembly, that is. It put forth proposals which were later on confirmed by the -- commander of the Territorial Defence. Whether this procedure was implemented to the full or not, I can't tell you. I don't have that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would it be a convenient time, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The trial stays adjourned until 11.00 sharp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you may continue immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Budimir, I would kindly ask you now to take the document that is in front of you. The Trial Chamber has already asked you questions about this. Page 54 of the Official Gazette of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor, issue 2, year 1992, and please look at Item 55 again. In this item, the Crisis Staff of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor decided to relieve of his duties the commander of the Territorial Defence of Prijedor, Major Slobodan Kuruzovic. As you can see, the decision is dated 29th of May, 1992. Since from the document S141, which is minutes from the Assembly of the Serbian People of Bosnia and Herzegovina, we saw that the Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina was abolished on the 12th of May 1992, can we conclude that on the 29th of May, 1992, there was no republican commander of the Territorial Defence of the Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The assembly adopted the decision, but I have no information about the implementation of that decision and how it was actually done in practice. I'm talking now about the timing. I'm not questioning that this decision was made. I don't think that it made any sense to discuss it, and I don't think it made any sense to formulate it in this way if it had been already decided and the matter was already resolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So this enactment relates to the commander of the territorial part of the Territorial Defence, that is, the part related to Prijedor Municipality?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The commander of the TO, the territorial part, because the manoeuvreing part was headed by another commander, and it was subordinated to the army. It was headed by Commander Colic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you one thing you have already been asked about, and I just want a clarification. It has to do with the late Simo Drljaca. Is it true that you did not see Mr. Drljaca socially?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Because you were not there, you probably don't know who he spent Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. time with, his spare time, I mean. Just for clarification.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't spend time with him, and I don't know. But I did say in my previous testimony that Mr. Drljaca and Mr. Stakic and Mr. Arsic often spent time together. I didn't socialise with them, but I knew that the three of them did see each other socially.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have one thing to ask you that has to do with the transcript of this radio programme. I will read out. It is from Exhibit S91-1, page 4 of the B/C/S version. Mr. Kuruzovic says: "At 5.00, representatives of our Serbian authorities came to see me in the command headquarters. President of the municipality, vice-president of the municipality, chairman of the executive committee, secretary for the economy, defence minister, and all the others according to their respective departments in the municipality, and then we began dispatching them their separate ways. There were also a few prominent company directors there." You mentioned this when you came to Cirkin Polje, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: His Honour asked you where your office was located, and you said it was in the building of the Ministry of the Interior in 1992. Apart from the section that had to do with the centre for alerting, your office was in the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was in the same building in the annex, which belonged to the secretariat for defence. Two-thirds of the building belonged to the Ministry of the Interior, and one additional wing that was built later belonged to the organ that I worked for.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you for this additional explanation. However, you did mention that later on, your department of the Ministry of Defence moved. Did it move to the building of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor or to some other place further removed and how removed from the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the department, but the section. Section is a lower unit from the department. This section moved to another building near the Patrija department store. It used to be the building accommodating socio-political organisations, the municipal committee of the League of Communists, the socialist alliance, the league of the socialist youth and other organisations. We occupied the lower part of the building -- sorry, they occupied the lower part of the building, and the part of the building that we got was allocated to the Ministry of the Interior. It was perhaps 800 away from the existing building of the Ministry of the Interior. I can't be precise. I didn't measure it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I didn't expect you to quote the exact distance anyway. Thank you very much. Page 21 of yesterday's transcript, the 127th day of trial, there was talk about the agenda of the Crisis Staff. You explained that it concentrated mainly on general issues moving on later to specific discussion. Do you know, perhaps, whether the members of the Executive Board participated in the preparation of various items in this agenda?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the preparation of the agenda, I already said that there were no particular preparations. As for general issues discussed, all members of the Executive Board, depending on the issue under discussion, participated. If something had to do with socioeconomic issues, then Mr. Travar took part, Mr. Pavicic took part when issues from his province were discussed. If something relating to defence was in question, then I would talk.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The sessions of the Crisis Staff that you attended, were they sometimes chaired by the late Dr. Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally speaking, I think that Mr. Savanovic usually stood in for Dr. Stakic. I don't rule out the possibility that certain sessions were chaired by Dr. Kovacevic, because according to the logic of things, generally speaking, he was the man who could have chaired meetings. Perhaps there were situations when Mr. Savanovic was absent, and I don't really know whether there was an agreement between Savanovic and Kovacevic as to which one of them would chair sessions. I can't know how often that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like the usher now to show the witness the document marked as S152, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a document issued by the public security station in Prijedor allegedly signed by the chief of the public security station, late Simo Drljaca. Could you please look at this document and tell us whether you had ever seen it before.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw this document before, nor did I participate in any session of the Crisis Staff discussing the documents you're asking me about and producing here. I don't know what this is all about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We won't be needing this document any longer. Mr. Budimir, your municipal secretariat for national defence, could it have declared mobilisation, or did this instruction have to come from a higher level, from a different level?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mobilisation could only have been declared by the competent authority authorised to do so by law, and it could not have been the municipal secretariat for national defence. It was not authorised to declare mobilisation by any means.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We agree with you. But I would kindly ask you to tell us which authority, which organ, was authorised to do so?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: President of the republic through the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since you know this area so well, some questions will surely sound odd to you, but in view of the case before this Tribunal, we have to ask them. Please tell us, could the Municipal Assembly declare mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could the Crisis Staff do that, the Crisis Staff of the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is a well-known fact that many people failed to respond to the mobilisation callup in 1991. And you told us that those people were not prosecuted. No repressive measures were taken against them at that time. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true. Those who, in keeping with the existing laws, were supposed to take such measures did not do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And if someone failed to respond to the mobilisation callup, did that person continue to be required to respond?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, until the law changed. As long as that legal requirement exists.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, if you can remember, under what legislation did your organ work, the municipal secretariat for national defence?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The municipal secretariat for national defence operated under the law on all people's defence. The Official Gazette was dated year 1983. And also, under the federal law on defence from 1983. There were also bylaws and instructions that regulated in detail the affairs, the purview, and authorities of these organs such as their authorisation to recruit, to reinforce units, to mobilise, et cetera. I am saying what the situation was until the adoption of the law on defence and the law on the army adopted by the Assembly of the Serbian People of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: These changes happened in June 1992, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1st of June 1992 was the date when these two laws were adopted. I believe the Official Gazette was 7/92.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The Official Gazette of Republika Srpska, you mean?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As a municipal body, you said you operated until the 1st of August 1992 due to the transition as of the 1st of June 1992.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under the law, the changes were supposed to take place immediately. But the organisational changes in the concerned bodies in terms of the staff and the organisation as well as decisions to replace some people and to change their status, all these changes were completed on the 1st of August. I, for instance, had a decision as head of the department for national defence that actually put me on this job on the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 1st of August. But these changes were officially proclaimed on the 1st of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As a municipal body, were you required to submit any reports to the Executive Board of the assembly of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under the previous law, regulated that the municipal body was required to submit reports to the Executive Board and the Municipal Assembly on certain issues envisaged by the law. And on other issues, annual reports had to be submitted covering all the aspects of the work of that body and all the facts relevant, which were conditionally speaking secret. On the municipal level, such reports had to be submitted to the republican level because that was the body controlling the municipal level and the municipal body in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which of these two bodies gave you instructions and orders?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depending on the issue in question, depending on the issue and who had competence for it. The republican secretariat was competent for issues related to the army. They gave us plans regarding replenishment and reinforcement. We as the municipal body only informed them of the movements of the men; so many were recruited; so many were sent to military drills; so many responded to callups, et cetera, et cetera. We didn't organise it, we just implement it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The purpose of your body was to supply the army with troops and materiel goods, materiel and equipment as the term was?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The function of the secretariat was to reinforce the army with military conscripts and materiel and equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, how did the army communicate their needs to you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: These needs were communicated at the level of the Ministry of Defence. This was integral communication. And then this was broken down and sent to -- first to Banja Luka, to the department of defence in Banja Luka, which then broke down that information into various units. And this department, as the second level in the organisation of the Ministry of Defence, would submit the information to us, and we acted on that information, and we reinforced the units in the territory of Prijedor Municipality. We also did it elsewhere, not only in Prijedor but also in Banja Luka, depending on where units were located. So from a higher level, we would get a breakdown according to which we would then reinforce all of our units with both troops and materiel and technical equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we then conclude that the army never communicated its needs either through the Municipal Assembly or through the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are talking about the brigades, the 43rd Brigade and others, they never communicated directly to us. They would communicate it towards the Ministry of Defence, and then the Ministry of Defence would inform the departments, and the departments would then inform us about the requirements for troops and the materiel and technical equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that your municipal secretariat for national defence could not command the troops, the army?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The municipal secretariat for national defence did not have any authority to command anybody or anything. It didn't have any instruments of coercion. It didn't have any people that would enforce anything. We only had nine people working in our agency, and three people in the information centre. That was all I had. I didn't have any other authorities, neither me personally nor my agency had any authorities or competencies towards any other organs or bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have to ask you whether that means that your agency could also not command the police, the Territorial Defence, the civilian protection? Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that when I answered your previous question. But let me just explain the term of "civilian defence." We as a body participated in the preparations and reinforcements of the ranks of the civilian protection. But at the level of the municipality, there was a municipal staff for civilian defence, and its commander was the vice-president of the Executive Board. From -- so we were in charge of preparations, and the command was given to the commander. So we couldn't command civilian defence. It was the commander who did that, and he received his orders from the district staff for the civilian defence, and the district staff received their orders from the republican staff. And as for the other structures and bodies, we didn't have any authorities over any of the bodies or organs that you have asked about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Budimir, you or your employees controlled companies and institutions during the times of peace in order to see whether they comply with the laws and obligations prescribed by various regulations dealing with the requirements of national defence?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The law on national defence regulated the competency and authority of the secretariat to inspect the preparedness for national defence of companies and other legal entities. A certain period of time I spent working as an inspector who was in charge of carrying out inspections. But this is such a complex issue, and I don't have the time to now go into details about all the plans that the companies had to draft. They had to draft plans for exceptional conditions, extraordinary conditions, plans for supplies under extraordinary conditions. So there were all sorts of plans that I don't think I have the time to go into details of all of these. If you have to ask me something more specific, I will gladly answer, but this question was too general.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My next question would be the following: Is it correct that you did not have the right to command over any of these companies and institutions in this sense?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you say "you," I don't know what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I apologise. As the municipal secretariat for national defence?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. We could not command anybody. When we noticed as inspectors that certain companies did not comply with the regulations, we could only issue a decision and a ruling that they should rectify their procedures in order to comply with the regulations. And then when they received this decision, they could appeal to a higher institution. But they usually did not complain because they respected our professional opinion, and they would rather put things right when they were told that there were things to be put right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the army had its own lines of supply, that they had other lines of supply outside of the requirements that went through the secretariat for defence?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army never sent requests to the secretariat for national defence about their supplies. What they sent us were requirements for the reinforcement of troops in particular units. As for the supplies, the quartermaster supplies, the army had its central quartermaster supply, and as the secretariat we had nothing whatsoever to do with the supplies for the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct, and would you agree with me when I say that your secretariat never supplied either the army or the police or the Territorial Defence or the civilian protection with weapons and ammunition?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to go back --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have to clarify some things, and we are taking the opportunity of you being knowledgeable about things.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We never supplied anybody with ammunition, weapons, food, or anything similar. The only thing we did as an organ of -- municipal organ, we reinforced units and Territorial Defence with troops. And we also carried out assignment of every conscript to companies, institutions and other legal entities, and we also deployed conscripts into the units of civilian protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was the form of the orders that you received from the higher instances of your secretariat, later on the ministry? Were these orders or decisions or what?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the documents that arrived in the secretariat for national defence were in the form of orders. I'm not ruling out the possibility that there were some other kinds of documents, bearing in mind the administrative nature of our organ. We also had the authority and competencies to deal with the issues of all the conscripts in terms of their ability for the army, whether they were able to serve the army or not. So these documents were not orders. But I believe that you're asking me about the documents that arrived from higher instance -- institutions, and these arrived in the form of orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was it customary for such orders that you received from your superiors, from the secretariat of national defence, later on from the Ministry of Defence, would contain the addressee and what measures should be taken?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The orders which arrived in my organ, since we had professionals working across the board, and these professionals knew what state documents were, regardless of their form, whether they were orders, decisions, conclusions, or any other. All of these documents should have contained a number, the date, the addressees, which actions were required, specific deadline by which these measures were supposed to be taken, who the documents were to be delivered to, and who should be informed about the implementation of the order that has been received.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like to go back to the question of mobilisation. Would you kindly explain to us whether the callup papers or replenishment and reinforcement of units were delivered by the military police or by the civilian police, that is, the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The department of the Ministry of Defence, and earlier on, the secretariat for defence, were not delivered either by the military police or by the civilian police. The conscripts received their callup papers through a courier service that was established as a service of this organ. These people who were couriers were also conscripts, and they worked in the part of town where -- with which they were familiar. They would receive callup papers from the officials in charge of mobilisation, and they were the ones who delivered those callup papers to the conscripts. It was their obligation to hand-deliver the callup papers and report whether they found the conscript at home or not. In case the conscript was home but refused to take the callup paper, then we, as the body, would ask the police to bring this particular conscript to our department for national defence, and later on to the unit to which he was assigned. And that was only the case if the conscript was found at home but refused to take the callup paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the spring and summer of 1992, your secretariat, and later on the department of the Ministry of Defence, did it participate in the reinforcement of the units of the Ministry of the Interior with men?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The municipal secretariat for national defence, from 1991 when the mobilisation of the units and structures of the army started, also started developing the reserve police units. The municipal secretariat headed by my predecessor Mr. Medunjanin carried out mobilisation of the reserve units of the police. But it did not carry out the mobilisation of the army. At that time, it carried out the mobilisation and reinforcement of the units of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Mr. Budimir, in the interest of the time, I would ask you to only answer the questions put to you, and the question put to you was related to spring and summer of 1992 only.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In any case, thank you, Mr. Budimir, for this additional explanation. I would now like to ask you whether you can explain to us who was it who decided about military assignment? In other words, who would be given what assignment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: During which period of time, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you can explain whether the same regulations were in force before the 30th of April and after the 30th of April 1992. Let's say throughout the entire 1992.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the military assignment, it was not a decision by -- made by any individual. It depended on who was trained for what during their compulsory military service, and it was based on their physical abilities. There were professionals who decided on that depending on people's military occupation. There were professionals who decided on that in keeping with the military occupation of the people who were at their disposal throughout all that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you're talking about professionals, are you talking about the professionals affiliated with your organ, the secretariat for national defence?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the secretariat, and later on at the department of the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you something about the work obligation. Do you remember who was it who drafted plans on work obligation?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Companies, institutions, and other legal entities. They would deliver their plans to us with their requirements. We did not have to respect their requirements to the full. But as much as we could, we respected their wishes. However, you have to know that we had to meet the needs of the army and the police and the Territorial Defence first. And it was only then when we could meet the requirements of companies and institutions for people who would be assigned to work obligation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You became a member of the Executive Board of the Serbian Assembly of the Municipality of Prijedor after the takeover, which was on the 30th of April 1992. You became a member because you were the head of the municipal secretariat for national defence.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not the head of the secretariat; I was an assistant for civilian affairs. And I've already said that I became a member of the Executive Board as the secretary of the municipal secretariat. So it was my function that entitled me to membership in the Executive Board.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, up to when were you a member of the Executive Board of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor and why you stopped being a member?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a member up to the 1st of August 1992, and then by the decision of the Ministry of Defence, I was appointed the chief of the department of the Ministry of Defence. Thus, I became an official of a state organ. I stopped being an official of a municipal body. As a state body official, I could not be a member of a municipal body. These two were incompatible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The rule according to which state officials could not be members of a municipal body was in force even before the 30th of April, 1992. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For that same reason, army officers and Ministry of Defence officials could also not be members of the Executive Board of any Municipal Assembly. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, I would like to ask you something about the National Defence Council. Whose organ was the National Defence Council?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The National Defence Council was one of the organs of the Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was the main role of that body?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already explained that, so I'll be brief this time because the Presiding Judge has already drew my attention to the time. The role was to consider the issues from the authority of the municipality and put forth proposals with this regard. Obviously, the issues relative to defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could this body make decisions with executive force?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The Municipal Assembly, was that a body which adopted decisions on the issues on which proposals were put forth by the National Defence council?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The National Defence Council formed opinions, put forth proposals and submitted those through the assembly. And the assembly could take those into consideration, and only adopt those decisions which were in keeping with the law on national defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if the meetings of this body were attended by people who were not its members? If you remember the minutes of a meeting of this body, the meeting that took part on the 15th of May 1992, this meeting was attended by three representatives of the army. And there was also Mr. Simo Miskovic there. Also Milenko Rajic was there. Were these people guests at the meeting, and do you know what their role was? Can you tell us something about that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that after the elections which took place in 1990, the assembly never appointed people to the defence council in keeping with the act on defence. And that is probably why, depending on the issue that were on the agenda, there were other people present at the meetings because the issues that were discussed were never classified. They were something that other people could be informed about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You've told us that this is the -- one of the bodies of the Municipal Assembly, and earlier on, you told us that this body was not in session during the existence of the Crisis Staff. However, while this body was active, and that was the first half of May, did the army inform the members of this body on its operations and activities? Did the army inform this body about classified information, about things which were classified as military secrets? Can you tell us something about that.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army, under no regulation, had the obligation to inform the Council for National Defence on those issues. And the army never did inform the council on any of such issues. According to the law, all of its obligations and activities, the army had to coordinate with its superior command. And it was from that command that it received orders for the -- for carrying out its actions and operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Budimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe now is the time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. May I ask the usher, please, to escort the witness out of the courtroom. As to the fact that this Trial Chamber discusses administrative matters and other issues under the rules designed to be part of Status Conferences, I reviewed the transcript, and I found out that it's time, and it is necessary once again, to address you Dr. Stakic in person by asking you whether you have any complaints about the situation in the United Nations Detention Unit; and in addition, whether you have actually any health problems.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no problems. Half a day work is okay, and I can cope with that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the defendant. We can't hear the defendant.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have been informed that Mr. Pavic has arrived, and he is a member of my Defence team. But he has not visited me yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In the meantime, it was once again cross-checked, and there is -- at least there should be no obstacle for a monitored visit by this member of your Defence team. So I think it would be appropriate, if there is -- should be any obstacle, then the Defence should alert us on this and giving the concrete names of persons denying the access of these persons to the United Nations Detention Unit. But what about the situation in the United Nations Detention Unit as such? Are there any actual problems in the moment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. There are no problems at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This concludes this morning's hearing. After the break, we'll restart. The trial stays adjourned until 30 minutes past 1.00. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.04 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Budimir.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During the war, that is, after April 1992, in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Republika Srpska, and in Prijedor, was there a terminology dividing or making a distinction between military and civilian authorities?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a general question. I personally based my testimony on the laws and regulations. In the army, there are no authorities, and as far as I'm concerned, the term "military authorities" from the legal point of view does not exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is there a term "civilian authorities"?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Authorities exist. Legislative authority, executive authority, and judicial authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I will not keep you on this ground any longer?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the usher to show Exhibit S107 to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you have this document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This document is dated 30th of May 1992, signed by Simo Drljaca. From the first sentence in this document, can you see that the first person singular is used in relation to the person issuing the order? In other words, does it say "I order the following..."?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the same sentence, I know you are not a language expert, if there is any decision by the Crisis Staff mentioned in this sentence, wouldn't it be correct to interpret that there is a decision by the Crisis Staff for or relating to rapid and efficient restoration of peace, and not securing of these facilities --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... of a hypothetical nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's not in the transcript. But did I hear that the question is not admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: That is correct. It should read: "Question not admitted because of its hypothetical nature."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But discussing about this document, we always had hypothetical nature of questions relating to whether there was the decision of the Crisis Staff or whether there was not a decision of Crisis Staff regarding this issue. And many questions have been asked relating to this question. So if I may reformulate my question and try to ask the witness his opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Budimir, I'm saying this again, if you can tell us, how do you see -- how do you understand the meaning of the first sentence in this document? What could it possibly refer to? What could the decision of the Crisis Staff, if any, refer to?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already said that I do not wish to express my own views and comments. I can only talk about the documents. And when the Presiding Judge asked me about this document, I made my view clear and said that I don't know about such a decision of the Crisis Staff. And what is written here and in which form, I really don't want to comment on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In Item 3 of this document, there is a reference to three names. Item 3 reads: "Further work and the selection of detainees shall be continued by a mixed group of national, public, and military security investigators. They shall be organised respecting the same principles of equal representation. Mirko Jesic, Ranko Mijic, and Lieutenant-Colonel Majstorovic shall be responsible for their work." First of all, let me ask you, was any of these persons a member of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the decision on the organisation and establishment of the staff, you can see clearly the composition of the staff. It proceeds from that that none of these persons were members of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could the Crisis Staff issue any orders to members of the national, public, or military security?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already answered a similar question saying that the Crisis Staff had no competencies or powers over the police or the army, and the bodies you mentioned are an integral part of the police and the army. It follows, therefore, that the Crisis Staff could not issue any orders to the Ministry of the Interior or the VRS, the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In Item 11 of this document, could you please turn the page and look at Item 11, we read, and it refers to the three persons mentioned above: "The security services coordinators shall submit every day a report on the preceding 24 hours to the chief of the Prijedor public security station at 1200 hours or when the circumstances allow no delay, they shall do so immediately." Did you see that the organisers -- coordinators of these services ever submit a report of this kind to the Crisis Staff of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never seen any such report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In Item 12, we can read: "The chief of security shall proceed in the same way with regard to the operation of the security services and security problems, if any." Have you ever received a similar report, a report of that kind, from the chief of security in the Crisis Staff of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't receive all the documents that were addressed to the Crisis Staff, but such a document never passed through my hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In Item 15, which is on the following page, if you would be so kind as to turn, please, the chief of the public security station, Simo Drljaca, orders: "I strictly forbid provision of any information whatsoever concerning the functioning of this collection centre. All official written documents shall be kept at the collection centre and may be taken out of it or destroyed only upon the approval of the chief of the Prijedor public security station. This shall be the responsibility of the security staff." Is this one of the parts of this document relating to the rest of the documentation indicating that outside of this centre, it was not known what was going on, so you, in the Crisis Staff, did not know what was going on in the Omarska investigation centre either?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot draw any conclusions on why and how. I can only say that I never had these documents before me, nor did I attend any sessions of the Crisis Staff that possibly discussed these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
